title: ABM FinServ Landing Page Copy Draft (Regulated Workloads) — v1
content:
Doc purpose
- Draft copy for FinServ regulated workloads landing page (ABM pilot).
- Audience: security + platform stakeholders at banks, wealth, payments, and regtech.
- Goal: book qualified meetings and shorten security review by making deployment boundaries + controls clear.

Status notes / open items
- Needs final Security/GRC review of retention language (do not imply “no logs” or “we never store data” without qualifiers).
- Need product sign-off on what’s GA vs limited availability for Private/on-prem packaging.
- Add proof points once we choose: benchmark snippet, customer quote (if approved), or “Redwood-verified performance profiles” statement.

Page structure (recommended)
1) Hero
2) Why Redwood for regulated inference (3–5 proof points)
3) Common FinServ workloads (use cases)
4) Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + decision guide (focus on Dedicated vs Private)
5) Security & compliance highlights + link to addendum
6) Reference architecture teaser (Private/VPC)
7) CTA block (schedule security+architecture review)
8) FAQ (objection handling)
9) Secondary CTA + contact

-------------------------------
HERO SECTION

Headline variants (pick 1 for A/B tests)
H1-A: LLM inference for regulated financial services—without sacrificing latency or control.
H1-B: Run production LLM workloads in FinServ with predictable performance and deploy-anywhere flexibility.
H1-C: High-performance LLM inference for FinServ teams with strict security and audit requirements.
H1-D: Dedicated and Private LLM inference for financial data—built for security review.

Subheadline variants
Sub-A: Redwood Inference helps security and platform teams deploy LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options—so you can meet audit, residency, and isolation requirements while keeping throughput and costs predictable.
Sub-B: Ship LLM features with a production-grade inference runtime plus the deployment boundaries FinServ requires: dedicated capacity, VPC options, audit logging, and customer-managed key integrations.
Sub-C: A developer-first inference platform designed to make security review and production rollouts faster—across hosted, dedicated capacity, and VPC/private deployments.

Hero bullets (3 bullets; keep crisp)
- Predictable latency and throughput for customer-facing workloads
- Deployment flexibility: Hosted → Dedicated → Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Security-forward controls: audit logs, encryption, SSO/RBAC, key management integrations

Hero trust line (optional; keep generic for now)
Option 1: Built for teams that need performance + auditability for regulated data.
Option 2: Designed to support security review with clear data boundaries and deployment options.

Primary CTA button variants
CTA-1: Schedule a 30-minute security + architecture review
CTA-2: Book a Private/VPC deployment consult
CTA-3: Talk to an SE about Dedicated vs Private
CTA-4: Request the FinServ security FAQ addendum

Secondary CTA (link)
- See the Private/VPC reference architecture
- View deployment options
- Get the evaluation checklist

Form intro microcopy (above form)
- Tell us what you’re building. We’ll route you to a solutions engineer familiar with regulated FinServ deployments.

Suggested form fields (for Growth / MOPs)
- Work email
- Company
- Role (Security/GRC, Platform Eng, ML Eng, Product)
- Deployment interest (Dedicated, Private/VPC, On-prem, Not sure)
- Compliance drivers (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI, GLBA, internal)
- Notes (optional)

-------------------------------
SECTION 2: WHY REDWOOD (PROOF POINTS)

Section headline options
- Designed for regulated inference in production
- Production-grade inference for FinServ workloads
- Performance you can measure. Controls you can audit.

Proof points (choose 4–5)
1) Predictable inference economics
   - Token-level visibility into latency and cost drivers.
   - Controls to tune batching/caching and routing policies based on workload.

2) Deployment boundaries that match your risk posture
   - Hosted API for fast evaluation.
   - Dedicated capacity for isolation + predictable throughput.
   - Private deployments (VPC / on-prem options) for regulated environments.

3) Reliability and graceful degradation
   - Policy-based routing and fallbacks to keep applications online during capacity constraints.
   - Clear runbooks and observability for production operations.

4) Audit-ready operational posture
   - Exportable audit logs (see FinServ addendum for details).
   - Identity controls (SSO/RBAC) and administrative visibility.

5) Key management integrations
   - Encryption in transit and at rest.
   - Support for customer-managed key integrations in Private deployments (details shared in security review).

Note to reviewers: avoid stating specific certifications or hard commitments on retention windows on the landing page; keep it “see addendum / discuss requirements.”

-------------------------------
SECTION 3: COMMON FINSERV WORKLOADS

Section headline
- Use cases we see across banks, payments, and wealth

Use case cards (copy draft)
1) Advisor & agent assist
   - Real-time copilots for call centers and relationship managers.
   - Prioritize low latency and predictable throughput during peak hours.

2) Document and communication review
   - Review customer communications and internal documents for policy alignment.
   - Prefer dedicated capacity and clear audit trails for governance.

3) Knowledge search & retrieval augmented generation (RAG)
   - Grounded Q&A over internal policies, product docs, and research.
   - Needs consistent performance and observability to manage cost at scale.

4) Risk & compliance analytics
   - Summarization, classification, and workflow automation.
   - Often requires strict access controls and data handling boundaries.

5) Developer platform standardization
   - A single inference platform across teams and regions.
   - Deployment flexibility for different data sensitivity tiers.

-------------------------------
SECTION 4: DEPLOYMENT OPTIONS (FOCUS: DEDICATED VS PRIVATE)

Section headline options
- Choose the right deployment model for your data
- Hosted, Dedicated, or Private—matched to your security requirements

Intro paragraph
Redwood supports multiple deployment modes so teams can start quickly and evolve their architecture as requirements tighten—from evaluation in hosted environments to dedicated capacity and VPC/private deployments.

Decision guide (simple)
If you need…
- Fast evaluation with minimal ops → Start with Hosted
- Predictable throughput + isolation → Choose Dedicated
- Network boundary control + regulated data posture → Choose Private (VPC / on-prem)

Dedicated section (copy)
Title: Redwood Dedicated
Bullets:
- Dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput
- Data isolation appropriate for many regulated workflows
- Configurable autoscaling policies and burst options
- SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (as contracted)

Private section (copy)
Title: Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
Bullets:
- Private control plane with customer-managed networking
- Supports regulated environments requiring tighter network boundaries
- Integration points for key management and audit pipelines
- Align operational responsibilities with your platform team (we’ll map this in architecture review)

Deployment comparison (lightweight table copy)
- Isolation:
  - Dedicated: dedicated capacity + tenant isolation
  - Private: customer-controlled network boundary (VPC / on-prem)
- Networking:
  - Dedicated: managed endpoint
  - Private: private connectivity patterns and customer networking controls
- Security review readiness:
  - Dedicated: standard security package + addendum
  - Private: architecture review + evidence package under NDA as needed

Callout (important)
Not sure which deployment you need? We’ll do a 30-minute discovery to map your workload, data flow, and review requirements to the right model.

-------------------------------
SECTION 5: SECURITY & COMPLIANCE HIGHLIGHTS

Section headline options
- Built to support security review
- Security controls you can evaluate early

Bullets (landing-page safe, non-absolute)
- Audit logging: available with export options (details in the FinServ addendum)
- Encryption: in transit and at rest
- Access controls: RBAC and SSO options
- Data handling: clear boundaries by deployment model; we’ll walk through flows during review
- Residency and retention: options depend on deployment and region; see approved guidance/addendum

Primary link
- Download / request: “FinServ Security FAQ Addendum”

Microcopy under link
We can share additional evidence under NDA where appropriate.

-------------------------------
SECTION 6: PRIVATE/VPC REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE (TEASER)

Section headline
- Reference architecture: Private/VPC deployments for regulated workloads

Paragraph
See a reference design for network boundaries, logging pipelines, and key management integration points—plus an outline of operational responsibilities across Redwood and your team.

Bullets
- Network boundary + connectivity patterns
- Audit/log export patterns into your SIEM
- Key management integration points (KMS/HSM)
- Observability and operational responsibilities

CTA button
- View the Private/VPC reference architecture

-------------------------------
SECTION 7: CTA BLOCK (BOTTOM)

CTA headline options
- Get a Dedicated vs Private recommendation for your workload
- Accelerate your security review for LLM inference
- Talk to an SE who’s done regulated deployments

CTA supporting text
Bring your security requirements (audit logging, key management, residency/retention expectations) and performance targets. We’ll map a deployment approach and outline a realistic evaluation plan.

Buttons
Primary: Schedule a security + architecture review
Secondary: Request the FinServ security FAQ addendum

-------------------------------
FAQ (OBJECTION HANDLING)

Q1: Can we keep sensitive financial data within our network boundary?
A: Redwood offers Private deployment options (VPC and on-prem patterns) designed for tighter network boundary controls. We’ll review your target data flow and map the right deployment model during an architecture review.

Q2: Do you support audit logs and exports for governance requirements?
A: Yes—audit logging is available with export options. We’ll confirm the right configuration for your environment and share approved details in the FinServ security FAQ addendum.

Q3: What are your options for encryption and key management?
A: We support encryption in transit and at rest, and Private deployments can integrate with customer key management approaches. We’ll walk through options and responsibilities based on your deployment model.

Q4: What latency/throughput can we expect?
A: Performance depends on model, sequence lengths, and traffic patterns. Redwood is designed for production inference with cost/latency observability and tuning levers (batching/caching/routing). We’ll size an evaluation to your workload.

Q5: Dedicated vs Private—what’s the practical difference?
A: Dedicated provides reserved capacity and isolation with a managed endpoint. Private adds customer-controlled networking boundaries (VPC / on-prem options) for tighter regulatory requirements. We’ll help you decide based on data sensitivity and review scope.

Q6: Can we start small and expand later?
A: Yes—many teams evaluate quickly and then move to Dedicated or Private as requirements solidify. Redwood supports a Hosted → Dedicated → Private path so you can iterate without re-platforming your API integration.

-------------------------------
SEO / META (DRAFT)

Page title options
- FinServ LLM Inference (Dedicated & Private) | Redwood Inference
- Regulated LLM Inference for Financial Services | Redwood Inference

Meta description options (150–160 chars)
- Run LLM inference for regulated FinServ workloads with predictable performance and Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment options.
- Redwood Inference supports Dedicated and Private deployments for FinServ teams needing auditability, isolation, and predictable latency.

-------------------------------
NOTES TO DESIGN (for DES-211)
- Avoid heavy “compliance badge soup” unless we have explicit approvals.
- Include a small “Dedicated vs Private” selector/toggle with 4–6 rows max.
- Make the primary CTA consistent across page; secondary CTA links to security addendum.
- Add a short “What to expect” modal after form submit: (1) confirmation, (2) scheduling link, (3) what we’ll ask for.

NOTES TO MOPs / ROUTING (for ENG-2941)
- Route high-intent submissions (Private/VPC selected OR ‘Security/GRC’ role OR ‘GLBA/PCI’ drivers) to regulated SE queue + Slack #sales support.
- Attach UTMs to HubSpot properties (abm_vertical=finserv, abm_campaign=regulated_workloads_pilot, abm_asset=landing_page).

Compliance-safe language reminders (do not use)
- Avoid: “We do not store any prompts/outputs” (too absolute)
- Avoid: “HIPAA/PCI certified” unless formally verified and approved (use approved phrasing only)
- Avoid: “On-prem is GA” if it’s still limited availability (use “available for select regulated environments” or “supported with Private deployments—details in review”) pending product sign-off

Reviewer checklist
- Security/GRC: retention/residency wording, audit log statements, evidence sharing language
- Product: Private/on-prem packaging accuracy, feature availability (GA/beta)
- Sales/SE: CTA alignment with meeting flow + common discovery questions
- Legal: any claims that imply certification/attestation
